findings.text: blocking: the added clause `and preferred not in lifted` (line 1270, with `and not _review_backend_excluded(preferred, config)` at 1271) rejects a preferred lane that is under a budget lift in force even when no exclusion names it, so the owning or local lane loses its lead and, when it is not a configured backend, disappears from the ordering entirely. At the reviewed base the loop used `preferred not in excluded`, and `_review_excluded_backends` (line 1202) subtracts the lifted set before returning, so a lifted preferred lane was admitted; head drops it. This contradicts the function's own docstring added by this commit (line 1244-1245, "a lane under a lift in force still survives, because the fleet has opened it") and the evidence fragment's claim that "the lift guard is preserved: a lane under a lift in force stays available". No test exercises a lift with _ordered_review_lanes (grep of tests/ finds none), so the regression ships unguarded.

justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1271 now routes the preferred pair through _review_backend_excluded, so the goal is met, though the same edit also drops a lifted non-excluded preferred lane, a behaviour the goal does not imply.
justifications.reuse: the fix reuses the existing pair resolver _review_backend_excluded (line 1118) and the existing _lifted_backends (line 1138) rather than forking them, but the added `preferred not in lifted` clause re-implements a lift check that _review_excluded_backends (line 1202) already owns, and does so with the opposite polarity, so the lift awareness is duplicated rather than read from one owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py, tests/test_old_names_resolve.py, the evidence fragment) is inside the declared write paths and no other file changed.
